answer: Each identity anchors to a registered willow coppice on an island: one coppice, one vote. Each epoch the keeper sails a fresh voyage to the island and signs a nonce-bound reading — willow ring growth, GPS, and the ferry manifest entry. The registry checks each voyage against the published manifest; a shared log collapses to one vote and burns a $50 stake. A farm wanting 100 votes must lease 100 coppices at $120 a year each and sail 100 voyages at $35 a trip; each coppice needs one season of logged growth, never pre-ageable in parallel. No signed voyage, no vote; cost rises linearly with n.
